variants.headline: Government cannot pay its debts
variants.sub: The colony's government is unable to pay its debts.
variants.body:
The colony's government cannot pay its debts. The inability to pay is the central financial fact, not an invitation to invent the amount owed. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish this payment failure from unreported arrangements with creditors or a presumed cause of the government's position.

An inability to pay is a credit event, but it is not a complete balance sheet. Business readers should avoid guessing the exposure of a creditor or the terms of a restructuring. The disciplined approach separates the known failure from a recovery calculation for which this report supplies no figures.

We hold {target} to a critical standard. An inability to meet public debts is a fundamental failure of financial stewardship, and responsibility should not be displaced by an attractive description of the difficulty. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.

variants.sub: Government debt in the colony cannot be paid by the administration.
